title: Seen before it was built
after_why: the series line names the newest published report; 11 to 14 are drafts, not yet published
question: On 2026-10-20 Matthew asked for a dragon costume, fire to breathe and armour for the knight's horse. What did the two mock-ups show him before anything was built, what went out in 0.0.392, 81 minutes after he asked, and where does the game differ from them?
trigger: Matthew, that day, on the dragon mock-up at 13:46: “looks good.” then “please publish as a du_report.”; at 13:47, on the horse's: “include this too -- looks good”.

dragon.title: 🐉 A dragon costume and 🔥 six kinds of fire: a mock-up
dragon.what: The friend drawn by the game itself (the wolf suit, standing, facing right, recoloured), with the dragon's pieces added: two horns and a row of spines on the hood, teeth along the hood's opening, a slit-pupilled eye on the hood, scales, a plated belly, three claws on each foot, flapping bat wings, a tapering tail with its spines up and a spade at its tip. Six fires on the big picture and as six cards; hold to breathe (a button, or F); four colour pickers; a sky (dusk, day, night); the pieces named; bubbles drifting in that the heat pops, and a count of them.
options: A wide stream that starts white-hot at the mouth, turns yellow, orange and red, and ends in smoke.
Balls of fire with flaming tails, shot one after another, that burst into sparks.
Two ribbons of flame, one red and one yellow, that twist around each other.
A narrow roaring jet, blue and white like a torch, with orange at its tip and sparks.
Toy flame pieces, see-through orange, yellow and red, that click on one by one and pop off.
Glowing bubbles with a flame inside that float out and pop into sparks.
dragon.credits: LEGO Castle: the Dragon Knights battle pack (2010) flame piece and plume, for the brick fire; the Dragon Suit Guy (Collectible Minifigures, 2018), the same idea as this costume; the Dragon Knights' dragon-head armour, to tie in with the horse (ticket 498).

horse.title: 🛡️ Armour for the knight's horse: a mock-up
horse.what: The game's own horse, as 0.0.390 drew it side on and ridden with its saddle on, in six sets that take the knight's arms: two colours, a layout (quartered, halves, plain) and an emblem (none, falcon, crown, cross, chevron); four coats (white, grey, brown, black). The plume sways.
options: Steel all over: a chanfron down its face, plates down its neck, a chest plate, side plates and a rump plate, and a plume.
A steel face plate and a cloth in the knight's arms to below its belly, with a scalloped hem and the emblem on its side.
A cloth in the knight's arms over everything: its head (eye holes, ear sleeves), its neck, and down to its hooves.
A dragon's head for a chanfron (horns, spikes, teeth), scaly neck plates, and a cloth with a dagged hem.
One chunky helmet with round eye holes and a plume in a clip, as on a toy horse, and a short cloth over its back.
No armour: rosettes and ribbons on its bridle, a plume, and a saddle cloth with tassels in the knight's colours.
horse.key_note: The mock-up's key for the toy helmet is "lego"; the game's is "toy".
horse.credits: LEGO Castle: the horse battle helmet with a plume in Knights' Kingdom (6095), for the toy helmet; the cloth barding of the Lion Knights' Castle (10305), for the half caparison; the Dragon Knights' dragon-head armour, for the dragon helm. The real pieces' names: chanfron (face), crinet (neck), peytral (chest), crupper (rump), flanchards (sides), caparison (the cloth).

heat.about: How far each fire's heat reaches from the mouth, in the friend's units (standing, the friend is about 460 of them from the top of the hood to the soles), and its half-angle in degrees. The mock-up's HEAT is the game's FIRE_HEAT.side, number for number; front (a disc about the mouth, its radius) and away (a cone up from the head) are the game's own.
heat.source: mockups/dragon-fire.html HEAT; dress-up/js/08-body.js FIRE_HEAT at dress-up-0.0.392

differences: Six fires: roaring flame, fireballs, twisting fire, blue-hot jet, brick fire, fire bubbles
All six, by the same names, in 🎮 Controls, “🔥 its fire” (the roaring flame to start with). Side on, the same shapes, moved by the same timings
Drawn three ways, each a drawing of its own: side on; toward us, out of an open “O” mouth; away, rising past the head
Hold a button or F to breathe; “tap it for a puff”
Held: 🔥 on the game controller (the right trigger), on the screen's controller, or F. Let go, it fades in 0.2 s; no puff of its own
From the 👄 mouth, the 🫲 left hand or the 🫱 right hand
The same three, “🧭 from where”; and a size, “📏 how big”, 50 to 200
The heat, a cone past the flames; bubbles drifting in pop
The same six cones side on; toward us a disc, away a cone. It pops the bubbles of bubble space, the bubble room, the bubble makers, the friend's blown ones and a diving suit's leaks
“🌡️ show its heat”, on to start with
A count, “🫧 popped by the heat”
Fire makers anything can use: a torch, a campfire, a cannon, a dragon placed in a scene
“🔁 keep breathing (for looking)”, the sky, “🏷️ name the pieces”
For looking at the mock-up; not in the game
The friend in a dragon suit, side on, standing
The same pieces, in 🐯 Costume after the deer; facing us, from behind and from the side; standing, sitting, lying, crawling and swimming
The same four, starting at the mock-up's; 6 to 8 swatches each and “any color”
“🪽 its wings”: flapping (with their own slow beat, or an LFO from the mixing board), open and still, or folded
Six sets: full plate, half caparison, tournament, dragon helm, toy helmet, parade
All six, by the same names, in 🧍 Body's 🐴 the horse, “🛡️ its armour” (none to start with)
Side on, from the front and from behind, each a drawing of its own; led and ridden
Cloth and plume in the knight's arms from 🐯 Costume, else the halter's colour
As proposed: a knight's horse in the knight's colours, layout, emblem and plume colour; otherwise the halter's colour and a lighter shade, quartered, no emblem
The arms and four coats, chosen on the page
Chosen where they already were: the knight's arms in 🐯 Costume, the coat in “🐴 its coat” (7 colours)
The plume sways all the time
Plumes and the parade's ribbons swing with the stride, as the tail does, and hang still while the horse stands
The 🎪 tournament's cloth over the whole head, with no bridle drawn over it
The bridle drawn over the head cloth, so the rein has its ring: its strap crosses the eye, and the noseband and the ring show
The dragon helm in a fixed green
The same fixed green; it does not follow the dragon costume's colours
Pieces placed on their own: a 🐴 chanfron on a stand in the armoury

checks.about: Each ticket's check (tools/checks/*.mjs) drives the released page in headless Chrome on GitHub's computers and prints one ok or FAIL line per thing it checks. Counted from the runs' logs.
ticket_checks: seven choices; every set different in every view, led and ridden; the arms' and the halter's colours; the frame holds plume and horns; the near hind leg in front of the tail; nothing over the rider's face

among the costumes; its colours start as the mock-up's; two wings, a tail with a spade in every facing; every tail spike up, crawling and swimming too; no wing through the floor; flapping, open and folded; every pose drawn

F held draws a moving fire, let go removes it; all six fires in every view; from a hand; the heat reaches past the flames and pops bubbles in reach, not out of reach; in the bubble room facing away and toward us; at most 10 a frame at size 200; the controller's button and the screen's

other_fails_0_0_392: a fence piece dragged with the pointer: the check read the piece where it was put after the drag
the led horse before the friend, and a count of the horse box's rows that more choosers had outgrown
the led horse's size against the grazing ones: the check measured a wrapper, not the horse
